programme.title: Erin Burnett OutFront
programme.desc: It's Erin Burnett's turn to step out front and try to maintain a viable viewer presence for CNN in the weekday news arena. But the former CNBC anchor won't worry about ratings for her hourlong general news program, comparing that burden to "death." Instead, she'll concern herself with translating world events into relevant information for viewers, paying close attention to such topics as the Middle East and women's issues. "I want people to say that our show is smart. I want our show to be authentic", Burnett says in a promo. "I want our show to have courage". Left unsaid, of course, is that she wants her show to have a big audience, too.

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Mark Wright and the team help foster carers Jenny and Chris make their small bungalow work for family life. With their living room doubling as a play space and home office, and a loft filled with unused rooms, the house no longer meets their needs. The team restore order upstairs, create a cosy reading nook for Jenny, build a dedicated work-from-home desk for Chris and rework storage around awkward spaces. Thoughtful design and smart fixes give this generous family room to breathe again.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Greek Job

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Hannah and Christie are a couple whose boxy 42-square-metre garden does not reflect their fun-loving lifestyle. Chris is a DJ, Hannah plays the sax, and the feel of a music festival would be a great theme for the team to include.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Things that go bump in the day, a booming new sport and one very pink footstool await Margie Cooper and Ishy Khan as their road trip rolls into Essex for its penultimate battle.

programme.title: South Pacific
programme.desc: Flightless parrots, burrowing bats, giant skinks and kangaroos in trees - on the isolated islands of the South Pacific, the wildlife has evolved in extraordinary ways. Island living can carry a high price, for when new species arrive, all hell breaks loose. There lies a puzzle: why do animals perfectly adapted to island life simply give up the ghost?

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are in Huddersfield in West Yorkshire, and experts Mark Stacey and Christina Trevanion are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. A beautifully crafted clock catches Christina's eye, while Mark is drawn to an unusual piece of Lalique glass. Meanwhile, Paul Martin pays a visit to Nostell Priory, a grand house that reveals a perfect marriage between Georgian architecture and craftsmanship.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Richard Osman takes to the host seat for a final week of quizzing before he hands over the baton to a new host next week. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday.

programme.title: South Pacific
programme.desc: The South Pacific is still relatively healthy and teeming with fish, but it is a fragile paradise. International fishing fleets are taking a serious toll on the sharks, albatross and tuna, and there are other insidious threats to these bountiful seas. This episode looks at what is being done to preserve the ocean and its wildlife.
